title: Household Add-On Membership: when a nonpayment suspension may become an administrative removal
content:
## Product and scope
This document states the Household Add-On Membership basis for how long an add-on suspended for nonpayment may remain suspended before it may be administratively removed.

## Rule
An add-on that has been suspended for nonpayment may be administratively removed only once that tier's past-due grace period has fully elapsed, counted from the moment the add-on was suspended. The grace period is counted in full calendar days, with no partial-day rounding: a day that has not yet fully elapsed does not count toward the grace period.

## Points of judgement
- The clock the grace period counts from is the add-on's own suspension, not the missed charge that caused the suspension and not any later date.
- "Full calendar days with no partial-day rounding" means a grace period is satisfied only once that whole number of complete days has passed since the suspension; a removal recorded before the grace period's full day count has elapsed is not authorized by this basis.

## Boundary case (illustrative only)
If an add-on's grace period for its tier is a given number of calendar days, and the add-on suspends on a given date, an administrative removal is not yet authorized on the day before that full number of calendar days has elapsed since the suspension, and becomes authorized once that full number of calendar days has elapsed.

The number of grace-period days in force for each add-on tier is recorded in that tier's own parameter basis.
